text.p: German telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom AG on Tuesday dismissed as pure speculation a report that it and the Italian power group ENEL would make a bid for information technology group Olivetti.

The economic daily Handelsblatt newspaper said in an advance copy of a story to appear on Wednesday that the two companies planned to make a bid for Olivetti in order to gain control of the company's mobile telephone holdings.
"This is pure speculation," a Deutsche Telekom spokesman said.
Olivetti holds a majority stake in the mobile phone group Omnitel Proto Italia, Italy's number two wireless communications group.
The Telekom spokesman, however, confirmed previous reports from Italian officials that it and ENEL planned to make a bid for Italy's third mobile phone licence.
Bidding for the Personal Communications Network (PCN) licence will begin next month and the licence is due to be awarded in December.

The tender was due to be offered earlier this year but was postponed for technical reasons. Some of the companies interested in the licence have complained that the delay has allowed Italy's existing mobile phone firms to strengthen their market position.

Italy currently has two Global Systems Mobile (GSM) phone operators -- state- controlled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) and Omnitel, managed by information technology group Olivetti through an international consortium.
